// Minimal CSV reader for the billing export.
function parseLine(line) {
  return line.split(",");
}

function parseCsv(text) {
  const lines = text.trim().split("\n");
  const header = parseLine(lines[0]);
  return lines.slice(1).map((l) => {
    const cells = parseLine(l);
    const row = {};
    header.forEach((h, i) => (row[h] = cells[i]));
    return row;
  });
}

module.exports = { parseLine, parseCsv };
// Prints every parsed row, then checks totals.
const fs = require("fs");
const { parseCsv } = require("./broken");
const rows = parseCsv(fs.readFileSync(__dirname + "/data.csv", "utf8"));
let total = 0, badRows = 0;
for (const r of rows) {
  const amt = Number(r.amount);
  console.log(`row ${r.id}: ${r.name} | ${r.city} | ${r.amount}`);
  if (!Number.isFinite(amt)) badRows++; else total += amt;
}
const expected = fs.readFileSync(__dirname + "/data.csv", "utf8").trim().split("\n").slice(1)
  .map((l) => Number(l.slice(l.lastIndexOf(",") + 1))).reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
console.log(`total=${total} expected=${expected} badRows=${badRows}`);
if (total !== expected || badRows) process.exit(1);
if (rows.find((r) => r.id === "245").city.indexOf(",") < 0) process.exit(1);
console.log("OK");

content.text:
I fixed the CSV reader in the `N03_csv` package, and its `test.js` now passes. The total matches the expected 2555295, there are 0 bad rows, and it prints `OK`.

**Cause:** `parseLine` in `N03_csv/broken.js` split each line on every comma, including commas inside quotes. A field like `"Chennai, South"` became two cells, so the amount column shifted and 16 rows lost their amounts.

**Fix:** `parseLine` now reads the line one character at a time and tracks whether it's inside quotes. It only splits on commas outside quotes, drops the surrounding quotes, and turns `""` into a literal `"`.

`parseLine` was the only change. I didn't edit any `test.js`, `run_all.js` or other package.

The parser still treats each line as one row, so a quoted field that contains a line break would still be split wrongly. Nothing in the current data does this.
